items.title: Guardian reviewer sessions isolate executor MCP projection
items.summary: Codex now keeps Guardian review sessions isolated from selected executor MCP servers while regular executor contexts retain their MCP projection. This changes a monitored tool/MCP/policy boundary consumed by local spec/.codex and TDD policy surfaces.
items.localContractImpact: Require executable compatibility evidence before adopting the new Guardian/executor MCP isolation behavior in local Codex policy or controller assumptions.

observations.observation: Since 76ceaddb29444388fbbbae07c46f7e8849f9658b, Codex changed core MCP/policy runtime; the current head explicitly prevents Guardian reviewer sessions from inheriting selected executor MCP-server projection and tests review behavior with unavailable executor MCP servers.

claims.text: Guardian review and normal executor MCP environments now have intentionally different server-projection behavior, so local policy compatibility must be established rather than inferred.

items.title: Codex app-server protocol and generated schemas advanced together
items.summary: Codex app-server protocol sources and generated JSON/TypeScript schema projections changed together across MCP event streaming, thread history/responses, configuration requirements and related notifications.

claims.text: Current Codex protocol and generated schema projections differ from the previous admitted baseline and must remain reconciled as one declared projection chain.

items.title: OpenTelemetry adds stable processor-visible record-only sampling
items.summary: OpenTelemetry Python adds stable AlwaysRecordSampler, converting DROP to RECORD_ONLY while preserving RECORD_AND_SAMPLE behavior. This creates a supported way to retain all spans for processors without forcing all spans to export.
items.localContractImpact: Account for RECORD_ONLY as a supported causal-observation configuration when designing ctrl telemetry collection; sampling still does not determine semantic admission or qualification.

observations.observation: AlwaysRecordSampler delegates to a root sampler and replaces Decision.DROP with Decision.RECORD_ONLY, retaining attributes and trace state while leaving sampled decisions unchanged.

claims.text: ctrl can observe processor-visible spans independently from export sampling when using this upstream facility, but telemetry remains observation-only evidence.

items.title: Astral analyzer type and reachability semantics continue to move
items.summary: Astral main advanced broadly across ty type semantics, constraints, reachability, parser/module-resolution and IDE surfaces; the current tip fixes invariant gradual tuple materialization ranges.
items.localContractImpact: Retain as forecast analyzer evidence for future CPython/local-probe correlation; do not promote inferred analyzer behavior to runtime truth.

observations.observation: The delta changes ty reachability/constraint/type machinery and the current head special-cases unrestricted variable-length tuple materialization in invariant specialization relations to avoid rejecting valid specializations.

claims.text: These are static analyzer observations and require CPython/local executable witnesses before any runtime or qualification conclusion.

items.title: GenAI instrumentation realization tightens provider compatibility bounds
items.summary: OpenTelemetry Python GenAI now enforces explicit lower/upper bounds for instrumented provider dependencies and pins latest test requirements, tightening the adapter compatibility envelope.
items.localContractImpact: Treat provider-version bounds as realization compatibility evidence for integrations/openai/packages/runtime, not as telemetry semantic authority.

observations.observation: Instrumentation packages now carry explicit upper as well as lower provider dependency bounds and latest test requirements are pinned to exercise those declared compatibility ranges.

claims.text: Provider instrumentation compatibility is narrower and more explicit, but the adapters remain observation providers rather than qualification authorities.

items.title: OTel-Arrow adds local retained-work accounting primitive
items.summary: The OTel-Arrow dataflow engine adds local retained-byte/unknown-item accounting and ownership tickets, but explicitly does not wire the primitive into runtime attribution, metrics, configuration, enforcement or production charge sites.
items.localContractImpact: Track as optional dataflow implementation evidence only; it does not change OTLP/OTAP semantic preservation or ctrl qualification gates.

observations.observation: A non-Send runtime-local accounting object tracks known retained bytes, unknown-size items, abandonment and arithmetic corruption; upstream explicitly states runtime wiring and telemetry export are not included.

claims.text: Retained-work accounting is an internal optional dataflow capability at this revision, not a change to canonical OTAP trace semantics or a qualification verdict.
